summary: Ignác Goldziher worked in religious studies and other fields. He studied at Eötvös Loránd University under Ármin Vámbéry, Humboldt University under Emil Rödiger, Leipzig under Heinrich Leberecht Fleischer (PhD ~1870), and Leiden. He taught at Eötvös Loránd University (PD 1872; professor 1894).

Igor Dmitrievich Serebryakov was an Indology and linguistics scholar. He studied at the Faculty of Philology of Saint Petersburg State University (~1935–1940). He held posts at the Military Institute of Foreign Languages, Pravda, and the Institute of Oriental Studies (~1960–1998).

Indologist Igor Dmitrievič Serebrjakov studied at Saint Petersburg State University under Fyodor Shcherbatskoy (~1935–1940). He was a teacher at the Military Institute of Foreign Languages (1941–1947) and a naučnyj sotrudnik at the Institute of Oriental Studies (1961).

Igor Mikhailovich Reisner was a scholar of history, archaeology, and Indology. He studied at the Special Faculty of the Frunze Military Academy and held a post at the Institute of Oriental Studies of the Russian Academy of Sciences (~1950–1958).

Ihsan Ali works in history, archaeology, and Indology. He studied at the University of Peshawar, the UCL Institute of Archaeology (MA ~1990), and under Frank Raymond Allchin. He held posts at Peshawar, Hazara University (Vice Chancellor ~2006–2009), and KP Archaeology.

Ikko Arai specializes in Buddhist studies and Indology. He completed a PhD at Komazawa University, studying under Shiro Matsumoto, Kazunobu Matsuda, Lambert Schmithausen (2004), Harunaga Isaacson, and Michael Zimmermann.
Ikuhisa Takigawa is an Indology and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Waseda University. In 2002, he was attested as a part-time lecturer (非常勤講師) at both Waseda University and Tokai University.
Ikuko Tazaki is a researcher in religious and Buddhist studies. In 2017, she was attested as a special researcher (特別研究員) at Otani University and an affiliated researcher (連携研究員) at Kyoto University.

Ikuro Hattori specializes in Indology, Buddhist studies, and philosophy. Holding a PhD from Pune University, he was attested as a researcher at the Nakamura Hajime Eastern Institute in 2003, and later as full-time researcher and lecturer at Aichi Gakuin University.
Ildikó Puskás was an Indologist and historian who studied under János Harmatta (~1961–1966). She held a post at Eötvös Loránd University from circa 1970 to 2009.

Ilkka Pyysiäinen is a religious studies scholar who studied under René Gothóni (~1985–1993). He served as an Academy Research Fellow at the University of Helsinki (1984) and held a post as a visiting researcher at the University of Oxford.

Ilya Gershevitch was an Iranian and Central Asian studies and linguistics scholar. He studied at Sapienza under Antonino Pagliaro, under Walter Bruno Henning, and Cambridge under Harold Walter Bailey. He held posts at Cambridge (1948–1965) and Columbia (1960–1961).

Immanuel Bekker worked in linguistics, history, and archaeology. He studied at the Martin Luther University of Halle-Wittenberg (~1803–1807) and held a post at the Humboldt University of Berlin (~1810–1871).

Imran Philip is a scholar in history, archaeology, and Indology. He studied for his doctorate under supervisor Kaustubh Mani Sengupta and held a Dr. Zakir Hussain Fellowship at The Asiatic Society (attested 2026).

Imre Bangha works in Indology and linguistics. He studied at Eötvös Loránd University and Visva-Bharati University (PhD 1998). He has held posts at Visva-Bharati (~1993–1998), the University of Oxford and Wolfson College (~2003), and Eötvös Loránd University (attested 2026).

Imre Galambos works in Sinology, Iranian and Central Asian studies, and history. He studied at ELTE, Nankai, and UC Berkeley (PhD ~2002). His posts include the British Library (2002–2012), Cambridge (2012–2023), Zhejiang University (~2021), and Hamburg (~2023).

Imre Hamar studied at Eötvös Loránd University, National Taiwan Normal University, and under Noritoshi Aramaki. He has held posts as a professor at Eötvös Loránd University (2006) and as a visiting professor at Otani University.
Imtiyaz Yusuf is a scholar of Buddhist and religious studies. He completed a PhD at Temple University (1984–1990) and held a professorship at the International Islamic University Malaysia in 2019.

In-gun Kang is a Buddhist and religious studies scholar. He studied at the Jesuit School of Theology, the Postgraduate Institute of Pali and Buddhist Studies under multiple teachers, and Heythrop College under Michael Barnes for his doctorate (attested 2012).

Indologist Indira Viswanathan Peterson studied at the University of Mumbai and Harvard University under doctoral supervisor Daniel H. H. Ingalls (~1973–1976). She held posts at Columbia University and Mount Holyoke College (~1983–2019).
